APPENDIX ( CZause 3.1 )
LEAF TEST

A

A-O.

The main objective of the leaf test is to evaluate the effect of different fabrics, fabric forms and drying times on filter yield. Varying dozes and types of chemicals should also be tested to establish chemical conditioning requirements. A-l. The leaf consists of a metal disc of about 30 cm2 area on which the filter medium is tightly fixed. The leaf filter is submerged in a sludge container of known solid contents. A chemical is added to the sludge in measured quantity and the sludge is kept stirred. A-2. The basic steps in performing a filter leaf test are as follows and should be repeated number of times to optimize the performance of each media tested: a) Condition the sludge in 90 to 25.0 litres containers. the

b) Submerge the filter leaf into the sludge slurry and operate vacuum pump for a varying time with varying vacuum. c) Gently remove the filter leaf from the sludge slurry cake to dry for a fixed drying time. 6
